currentContext.expansion: JBML's FY2025-26 expansion is concentrated in three named greenfield/brownfield sites plus incremental line additions. KHARKHODA, SONIPAT (HARYANA) - Plant J7, foundation stone laid Nov 2023: the first phase of construction and machinery installation is complete as planned and all requisite approvals for commencement of operations have been obtained; the Company has established a 1,600-ton robotic tandem line, a 1,000-ton progressive line, a weld shop and other supporting infrastructure, and plans are underway to install a 3,000-ton transfer press in line with MSIL's requirements. Supplies have commenced for the Brezza model relocated from Manesar to Kharkhoda, and production was initiated for the new Victoris model from September 2025; the plant continued to expand during the year with additional manufacturing capacity and supporting infrastructure, including advanced and flexible welding capabilities, to support a broader product portfolio. SMG SUPPLIER PARK, HANSALPUR (GUJARAT) - Plant J6, foundation stone laid Sept 2023: construction is complete as per schedule with all approvals obtained; a state-of-the-art weld shop has been installed to meet Maruti Suzuki's electric-vehicle production requirements and commercial production commenced in August 2025; a new manufacturing and assembly facility is being set up at J6 next to the customer's Hansalpur operations, adding press, weld and assembly capacity in line with the customer's Gujarat expansion, with work on readiness for production scale-up progressing through the year. SPARES DIVISION, PATHREDI, RIICO (RAJASTHAN): the first phase of construction is complete per schedule with statutory approvals secured; the requisite machinery and supporting systems have been installed to enable scalable operations serving growing spare-parts and service-component demand, with digital-system integration initiatives underway. MANESAR: manufacturing capacity was expanded during the year to meet increasing customer demand. FOR THE YEAR AHEAD, management states the expansion plan is built on business already awarded and on the higher demand baseline that settled in after the GST 2.0 reform, on two fronts - press-capacity expansion in NCR and Gujarat, and expansion of weld-assembly and overall plant capacity in line with new business awarded for new model programmes - each 'sized against confirmed customer programmes rather than a forecast'. The first response to the demand shift was to raise efficiency across press, weld and assembly lines 'to lift capacity without immediate extra capex'. Separately, the Company continues to expand tooling manufacturing capacity, having localised ultra-high-tensile dies for 1180 MPa parts (stated to be the only tool-room in India with such capability and scale) and is localising proto-dies and developing hot stamping dies within India. risks.risk: Single-customer and single-market concentration (Maruti Suzuki India Limited)
risks.note: Structural concentration disclosed in the BRSR rather than labelled as a risk: 'Jay Bharat Maruti Limited sells its products to Maruti Suzuki India Limited, which is an Automotive Original Equipment Manufacturer' is the entire stated customer description; exports contribute 0% of total turnover; markets served are 3 national states and 0 international countries; there are 0 international plants or offices. MSIL is simultaneously the customer, a Joint Venture partner with a Nominee Director on the Board, and the party in respect of which the Company is an Associate. The Chairman states plainly: 'the performance of our principal customer remains closely aligned with our own growth trajectory.'

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety (BRSR material issue 1 - Risk; financial implication: Negative)
risks.note: 'The company operates with a significant capacity for manufacturing, utilizing multiple processes and handling large steel components. A substantial number of permanent and contractual workers are employed at the plants, making occupational health and safety a critical issue.' Mitigation: a long-term objective of a zero-accident workplace supported by ISO 45001 practices, with the safety committee's performance monitored by top management. Note the workforce shape that makes this structural: 3,883 of 3,954 workers (98.2%) are 'other than permanent'.

risks.risk: Product safety and quality (BRSR material issue 6 - Risk; classified by the Company as a PRIORITY material risk; implication: Negative)
risks.note: 'Delivering defect-free, safety-compliant components is fundamental to sustaining our licence to operate in the automotive value chain. Any lapse whether a dimensional deviation or metallurgical flaw could trigger costly recalls, warranty claims from consumers and production stoppages at our OEM customers, eroding trust and market share.' Mitigated via IATF-16949 certified QMS, Poka-Yoke error-proofing and SPC at every workstation, FMEA and control plans, real-time digital dashboards, supplier audits and zero-defect training.

Flagged twice and by the customer itself. Resilience Scorecard: 'Variations in product quality across manufacturing locations can impact customer confidence and operational consistency, particularly at higher production volumes' - response is standardised quality governance, enhanced process controls, real-time defect monitoring and upgraded inspection systems across all plants. The customer scorecard rates Quality only MODERATE (outlook: STANDARDISE) with 'clear variation between plants and programmes... It is the variation, rather than the overall level, that is the focus.' [Provenance: Resilience Scorecard and customer scorecard were routed to the strategy_outlook / capex_expansion bundles, not risks_esg - back-filled.]

risks.risk: Execution risk in ramping new programmes and sizing capacity to demand
risks.note: Three linked Resilience Scorecard rows: 'Simultaneously scaling new customer programmes while maintaining existing production places significant pressure on capacity, resources and execution'; 'Sustained growth in customer demand requires rapid capacity enhancement. Delays in response could result in missed business opportunities and reduced market competitiveness'; and 'Capacity expansion must align with confirmed customer demand to ensure efficient capacity utilisation and avoid under- or over-investment.' Responses are phased ramp-up, process automation, collaborative planning with customers and suppliers, and sizing expansion against confirmed customer commitments. [Provenance: strategy_outlook / capex_expansion bundles.]

risks.risk: Responsible supply chain / limited product stewardship control (BRSR material issue 4 - Risk; implication: Negative)
risks.note: 'As an Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) tier-1 supplier, the company does not have direct control over product stewardship; however, it plays a crucial role in promoting sustainability throughout the supply chain.' Mitigated by an environmentally and socially sustainable supply chain built on policies and procedures, a supply chain policy guiding sustainable sourcing with preference to local suppliers, and awareness programmes covering 100% of value chain partners by value of business.

risks.risk: Greenhouse gas emissions and Scope 3 carbon accounting (BRSR material issue 7 - Risk; implication: Negative)
risks.note: The GHG reduction roadmap is aligned with the national Net Zero Target, with projections set for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions and a defined net-zero year; 'the company is diligently developing a comprehensive long-term mitigation plan' - i.e. the plan is not yet complete. The Resilience Scorecard adds the measurement gap: 'Achieving long-term decarbonisation goals requires accurate measurement of emissions across the value chain. Without reliable data, science-based targets and credible net-zero commitments cannot be effectively established.' [Provenance of the Scope 3 row: strategy_outlook / capex_expansion bundles.]

risks.risk: Workforce capability and attrition against an automation-led operating model
risks.note: Resilience Scorecard: 'A skilled workforce is essential to support automation, integration and real-time digitalisation. The pace of technology adoption can exceed workforce readiness, creating a capability gap' - addressed through structured learning, targeted automation training, digital tools, vision systems and AI-enabled inspection. The BRSR turnover-rate table shows permanent-employee attrition rising for a third year: 22.51% in FY2025-26 vs 20.90% in FY2024-25 and 18.21% in FY2023-24 (female permanent-employee turnover 33.33% in FY2025-26). Management's own third strategic priority is to reduce dependence on any single individual and strengthen middle management. [Provenance: Resilience Scorecard from strategy_outlook / capex_expansion bundles; attrition from BRSR.]

risks.risk: Water availability and quality (BRSR material issue 5 - Risk; implication: Negative)
risks.note: 'Water availability and quality are critical to uninterrupted operations across our manufacturing sites and to the well-being of our large blue-collar workforce. A shortfall - whether from drought, declining groundwater tables or tightening regulatory standards - could disrupt production schedules, raise treatment costs, and strain community relations, thereby impacting revenues and reputation.' The Company states its plants are not in any water-stressed areas, and has set site-specific consumption targets and installed ETP/STP treatment systems.

risks.risk: Human rights practices across a large contractual workforce and supplier network (BRSR material issue 2 - Risk; implication: Negative)
risks.note: 'Operations-intensive businesses typically involve managing a substantial employee and worker base in addition to a diverse supplier network. Consequently, the implementation of human rights practices is essential to mitigate social risks that could affect the organization and its value chain.' Addressed through established policies and procedures across all manufacturing units, extended to value chain partners.

risks.risk: Related-party concentration in both purchases and sales
risks.note: BRSR 'Open-ness of business' leadership indicator discloses that sales to related parties were 84.29% of total sales in FY2025-26 (88.04% in FY2024-25) and purchases from related parties were 56.93% of total purchases (53.89% in FY2024-25); investments in related parties were 73.49% of total investments made (75.37% prior year). Only the concentration percentages are carried here - the absolute rupee amounts are financial-statement derived and were not extracted. [Provenance: capex_expansion bundle.]

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

hero.oneLiner: Jay Bharat Maruti Limited (JBML) is a nearly four-decade-old tier-1 engineering and manufacturing partner to India's automotive industry, making stamped and welded steel structural parts, Body-in-White assemblies, rear axles and tools/dies almost entirely for Maruti Suzuki India Limited.
